own_scenes.desc: Holanda construyó su escena casi desde cero: Terrace (Stefan Robbers) buscaba la belleza tecnológica de lo más melódico de Detroit, frente al gabber ruidoso que vino después. Como antídoto, Marsel Van Der Wielen fundó Delsin en 1996 (primero para su alias Peel Seamus), con contrastes emocionales y acordes de navegar entre estrellas, portadas en blanco y negro como unas UR humildes e inspiración en el Retroactive y Planet E de Carl Craig (los discos de 69 y Piece) y en el Axis de Jeff Mills. Global desde el principio, apenas editó a dos artistas de Detroit, y quizá por eso pareció tan auténtico.

influences.name: Carl Craig: Retroactive y Planet E

refs.q: Delsin never went out of its way to fulfill the Detroit legacy, and perhaps that is why so many found the label to be so authentic.
refs.para: Delsin, like Plus 8, was also global very early on. In fact, for a Dutch label supposedly taking cues from Detroit, it odd to see that Van Der Wielen released records from only two Detroit artists, and only a half dozen or so from the Netherlands. Delsin never went out of its way to fulfill the Detroit legacy, and perhaps that is why so many found the label to be so authentic. Still it is an odd thing to be considered a standard bearer for a genre when its home base is still actively producing music.
